classes.name: HTTP, sessions and authentication
classes.invariant: The server knows which principal, session and request each credential belongs to, and no header, cookie, redirect or token the client controls can confuse that.
look: Cookie-authenticated state changes: a CSRF token or SameSite that covers this cookie, this method and this content type; JSON endpoints with cookie auth and no token.
Session fixation: is the session id rotated at login, privilege change and logout; are old sessions, refresh tokens and reset tokens invalidated on password change?
JWT: signature verified with a server-pinned algorithm and key; exp, aud, iss checked; kid or jku never used to pick an attacker key; decode-without-verify paths.
OAuth and OIDC: redirect_uri exactly matched, state bound to the session, PKCE where applicable, id_token nonce and audience checked.
Password reset and recovery: token random, bound to the user, single use, expiring; the reset link built from a trusted host, not from the Host or X-Forwarded-Host header.
Host and forwarded headers used for URLs, tenant routing or the client IP in rate limits; open redirects from next, return_to, redirect, url parameters.
CORS: a reflected Origin with credentials; a regex or suffix match on the origin.
Cookie attributes for a session cookie: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain and Path not wider than needed (only a hardening note without a reachable path).
classes.counts: A cross-site request changes state with the victim's cookie, a token is accepted for another principal or service, a reset link goes to an attacker host, a redirect lands on an attacker page after login.
classes.hardening: A missing cookie flag or header where another layer already stops the attack; a framework default you verified protects the route.

patterns.name: cookie set without HttpOnly or Secure
URL built from the Host header
CORS reflects the origin or allows all with credentials
login or reset without rate limiting signs

classes.name: Client-side and browser
classes.invariant: Attacker-influenced data (URL, fragment, message, storage, API response) never reaches a DOM, navigation or evaluation sink unencoded, and cross-window messages are checked by exact origin.
look: DOM sinks: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html, {@html}, bypassSecurityTrust*, jQuery .html()/.append() with data; what feeds them (location, hash, search params, postMessage, API text, user content)?
Navigation sinks: location.href / window.open / a.href from a parameter; javascript: and data: URLs.
postMessage handlers without an exact event.origin comparison (startsWith, includes, indexOf and regexes are not checks); postMessage(data, '*') carrying secrets.
Prototype pollution: a deep merge, extend or path-set over user keys (__proto__, constructor.prototype) followed by a gadget that reads the polluted property.
Tokens in localStorage or sessionStorage readable by any script on the origin; service worker caches of personalized responses across logout.
Browser extensions: content scripts trusting page messages; manifest permissions and web_accessible_resources wider than needed.
Framework escape hatches and markdown renderers with raw HTML allowed; sanitizer configured to allow dangerous tags or attributes.
classes.counts: A victim's session runs attacker script or data, another origin reads protected state, or a message from an untrusted origin triggers a sensitive action.
classes.hardening: A sink fed only by trusted literals or sanitized by a library you read; a missing CSP or frame protection where no sensitive action is framed.

patterns.name: deep merge or path set over user keys

classes.name: Supply chain, CI and release
classes.invariant: Nothing a contributor, a dependency author or a registry controls can run with the project's secrets, change what is released, or change what users install.
look: Workflows triggered by pull_request_target, issue_comment, workflow_run or fork events that check out the PR head and run its code or scripts, with secrets or a write token.
Expression injection: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}, .pull_request.title, .head_ref, .comment.body, .commits[*].message inside run: or a shell step.
Actions, images, tools and scripts pinned to a mutable tag (@v3, :latest, main) rather than a digest or exact version; curl | sh installers.
GITHUB_TOKEN permissions: write-all or contents: write where the job only needs to read; secrets passed to steps that print or upload the environment.
Caches and artifacts a low-trust job writes and a release job restores and executes.
Lockfiles: present, used by the install command (npm ci, pip install -r with hashes, cargo --locked), not ignored; install hooks (postinstall, build.rs, setup.py) of dependencies.
Release and publish steps: which branch, who approves, how the artifact is signed and how the installer verifies it.
classes.counts: A pull request or a dependency can run code with repository secrets or alter a release or an installer, with the full path shown.
classes.hardening: An unpinned action in a job without secrets and without write permissions; a missing lockfile with exact versions in the manifest.

patterns.name: expression injection in a run step
action pinned to a mutable tag
image pinned to latest or unpinned
sudo or root in a build

classes.name: Cloud, containers and deployment
classes.invariant: Each workload runs with the least identity, network reach and privilege it needs, and the configuration shipped is the configuration meant for production.
look: Containers: privileged, hostNetwork, hostPID, host path mounts, the Docker socket mounted, running as root (no USER in the Dockerfile), capabilities added.
Listeners bound to 0.0.0.0 for admin, debug, metrics or database ports; debug ports (--inspect, 5005, 5678) in a production command; ports published in compose for internal services.
IAM and policies with Action * or Resource *, public buckets or ACLs, security groups open to 0.0.0.0/0 on sensitive ports, wildcard CORS on storage.
Secrets in environment blocks, ConfigMaps, compose files, Dockerfile ENV or ARG, terraform variables with defaults, committed tfstate.
Development values that reach production: DEBUG, dev mode, disabled TLS, default passwords, an overlay that turns authentication off.
Serverless and edge: function URLs without auth, event sources trusted by body fields, broad execution roles.
classes.counts: An active configuration that exposes a sensitive service or credential to a lower-trust network, or lets a workload act beyond its role, with the consuming environment identified.
classes.hardening: A manifest for a local or test environment only; a missing restriction whose effect depends on a network or account policy you cannot read (needs_validation).

patterns.name: bound to all interfaces or a debug port

classes.name: LLM, agent and tool use
classes.invariant: Model output, retrieved content, memory and tool descriptions are untrusted input; every tool call is authorized for the requesting user on the named resource and bound to what the user asked for.
look: Where untrusted text enters the prompt (documents, web pages, emails, issues, tool results, other users' content) and which tools with side effects the same loop can call: a code-level check stands between them, or only the prompt?
Tool handlers: do they validate arguments as request input (paths, URLs, SQL, shell, ids) and re-check the requesting user's permission on the resource, or run with a service identity?
Confirmation flows: is the approved action bound to the exact tool name and arguments, or can a later turn, retry or changed argument run under the approval?
Memory and RAG writes: who can write what another user's session later reads; tenant filters in the retrieval query itself and in cache keys.
Model output rendered as HTML or Markdown with raw HTML, used as a URL, a command or a code path.
Secrets, other users' data or policy in the assembled context; MCP servers trusted by name or by tool description rather than by connection.
classes.counts: Attacker-controlled content causes a tool action, a disclosure or a write under another user's authority, or model output reaches a sink a user could not reach directly.
classes.hardening: A guardrail prompt that is weak but stands behind a deterministic check; an injection with no capability behind it.

patterns.name: tool arguments parsed from the model
markdown or HTML rendered from model output
secret in the prompt or context

classes.name: RPC, messaging and webhooks
classes.invariant: Every message is bound to an authenticated producer and the right principal, handled once, and authorized per item even in streams and batches.
look: Webhooks: signature or HMAC verified with a constant-time compare, over the raw body, with a timestamp window; the secret per sender; unverified handlers that change state.
GraphQL: introspection in production, no depth or complexity limit, batching, field-level authorization missing (a resolver that returns another user's node), mutations without auth.
gRPC and RPC: interceptors applied to unary but not streaming methods, health or reflection services, per-message authorization in a stream after the first message.
WebSockets: Origin checked at upgrade, authentication of the socket, per-message authorization, message size limits.

Queues and topics: can a producer choose another tenant's topic, routing key or reply queue; are message bodies trusted as control events (admin, provider callback); idempotency on redelivery; stale or out-of-order messages overwriting newer state.
Serialization: unknown fields, duplicate keys, default values and enum fallbacks read differently by two components.
classes.counts: A forged or replayed message is accepted as authentic, a stream or batch item escapes authorization, or a producer reaches another tenant's channel, with the effect shown.
classes.hardening: Introspection enabled without sensitive schema, a missing limit without a concrete amplification path.

classes.name: Memory safety, unsafe code and FFI
classes.invariant: Every length, index, lifetime and type assumption is derived from the worst accepted input, on both sides of every FFI boundary.
look: Fixed buffers and copies: strcpy, strcat, sprintf, gets, memcpy and read with a length computed from input; arithmetic before malloc (count * size, a - b) that can overflow or go negative; signed to unsigned conversions; off-by-one on terminators.
Lifetimes: pointers kept in callbacks, timers, caches or iterators after the owner is freed; realloc paths; error and cancel paths that free twice.
Rust unsafe: from_raw_parts, get_unchecked, transmute, set_len, raw pointer arithmetic; which invariant each block relies on and who checks it.
FFI: who allocates and frees, bytes versus elements, null and zero length, struct layout and repr, panics crossing the boundary.
Parsers of untrusted formats (images, archives, network frames): offsets and counts trusted before range checks; existing fuzz targets and sanitizer builds to run.
Concurrency: check-then-use on shared state without a lock, lock order, signal handlers.
classes.counts: A realistic untrusted input reaches an out-of-bounds read or write, a use after free, a type confusion or an unchecked unsafe assumption, shown by a harness, a sanitizer run or an unmistakable path.
classes.hardening: A pattern on data only the program itself produces; a panic (safe termination) in a non-shared process.

classes.name: Desktop, mobile and local IPC
classes.invariant: Only the intended principal can reach each local channel, bridge or deep link, and every privileged operation re-checks the normalized arguments.
look: Electron: nodeIntegration true or contextIsolation false with remote content; webSecurity false; ipcMain handlers that act on sender data without validating event.senderFrame or the arguments; shell.openExternal or openPath with a URL or path from content; custom protocol handlers; will-navigate and window-open guards.
Deep links and custom schemes: a URL from another app completes login, imports data or selects an account without binding to the current session; duplicate query parameters; replay.
Webview bridges (addJavascriptInterface, WKScriptMessageHandler, postMessage bridges): origin checked after every navigation, not only at load; bridge methods allowlisted and arguments validated.
Local sockets, named pipes, XPC, D-Bus, loopback servers: peer authenticated (uid, code signature, token), socket path permissions, world-writable directories, predictable paths.
Privileged helpers and installers: a low-privilege caller selects the command, path or user; symlinks and TOCTOU on files the helper writes.
Android: exported components without permissions, intent extras trusted, content providers with path traversal; iOS: URL schemes, keychain access groups, ATS exceptions.
classes.counts: Another app, another OS user, a sandboxed process or remote content reaches an operation meant for the app itself, with the operation shown.
classes.hardening: A setting that would matter only with remote content the app never loads; a channel reachable only by the same user with the same authority.

patterns.name: URL scheme or deep link handler

classes.name: Resource exhaustion and availability
classes.invariant: Untrusted work is bounded in size, depth, time and count before it costs the service anything shared.
look: Request bodies, uploads, JSON depth, array lengths, page sizes and query results without a limit; decompression of request data without a size cap.
Regular expressions built from or applied to user text with nested quantifiers or overlapping alternations (ReDoS); backtracking engines.
Outbound calls without a timeout (requests.get without timeout=, fetch without a signal, http.Client without Timeout); retries without a ceiling or jitter.
Work before authentication: expensive hashing, parsing, lookups or external calls on unauthenticated routes; missing rate limits on login, reset and signup.
Panics, unwraps, asserts and unhandled exceptions on input in a shared process; infinite loops on malformed input; recursive parsers.
Leaks: handles, temp files, subprocesses or connections not closed on the error path; detached work after a client disconnects.
classes.counts: One bounded request makes a shared service unavailable or costs far more than it should, with the amplification shown in code or a bounded local measurement.
classes.hardening: A missing limit with no shared resource behind it, a slow path reachable only by an authenticated operator.

patterns.name: unwrap or expect in a handler

classes.name: Data lifecycle, deletion and migration
classes.invariant: Deleted, revoked and migrated data stays deleted, revoked and consistent in every copy: primary store, caches, indexes, exports, queues and backups.
look: Soft delete: direct lookups, relations, search, object links and background jobs that ignore deleted_at; re-registration of a deleted identifier while references remain.
Revocation: removed membership, changed role, rotated secret or withdrawn consent not reaching sessions, caches, subscriptions, queued jobs or materialized views.
Migrations: old rows without tenant or ACL fields, defaults applied differently by old and new readers, dual-write windows, rollback paths restoring removed permissions.
Retention and deletion promises: queued work, exports, analytics, logs and backups that recreate or keep data after deletion.
Restore and undo: re-authorized with current policy, or restoring memberships, credentials and permissions as they were.
classes.counts: A deleted or revoked record, membership or credential still authorizes or is still readable through a path you traced.
classes.hardening: A copy that lags briefly by design with no authorization consequence.
